skills.name: Change the subject of a formula

note.text:
The subject of a formula is the letter on its own on one side: in v = u + at, v is the subject.
To make another letter the subject, treat the formula like an equation: do the same to both sides, undoing operations in reverse order.
• v = u + at → v − u = at → t = (v − u) ÷ a.
• A = πr² → r² = A ÷ π → r = √(A ÷ π).
• If the new subject appears twice, collect those terms on one side and factorise it out.
After rearranging, you can substitute values to find the new subject.

sections.heading: What the subject is
sections.text:
In the formula for the area of a rectangle, A = lw, A is the subject: it is alone on one side, and the formula tells you how to find it.
Sometimes you know A and w and want l. Then you rearrange the formula so that l is the subject: l = A ÷ w.
Rearranging is called changing the subject or transposing the formula.

sections.heading: Undo in reverse order
sections.text:
Look at how the new subject was built. In v = u + at, start from t: multiply by a, then add u.
To get t back, undo those steps in reverse order, on both sides:
• subtract u: v − u = at;
• divide by a: t = (v − u) ÷ a.
Keep brackets where you divide a whole expression. Squares are undone with square roots: A = πr² gives r = √(A ÷ π).

sections.heading: When the subject appears twice
sections.text:
In ax + b = cx + d, x appears on both sides. Collect the x terms on one side and the rest on the other: ax − cx = d − b.
Now take x out as a common factor: x(a − c) = d − b.
Divide by the bracket: x = (d − b) ÷ (a − c). Factorising is the key step.

key_words.meaning: the letter on its own on one side of a formula
rearrange a formula to change its subject
the operation that undoes another: + and −, × and ÷, squaring and square root

mistake.wrong: v = u + at → t = v − u − a
mistake.right: v = u + at → t = (v − u) ÷ a
mistake.why: a multiplies t, so undo it by dividing by a. Subtracting a would undo an addition.

worked_example.problem: Make t the subject of v = u + at, then find t when v = {v}, u = {u} and a = {a}.
steps: Subtract u from both sides: v − u = at.
Divide both sides by a: t = (v − u) ÷ a.

cards.idea: Undo the operations on the new subject in reverse order, doing the same to both sides.
To undo a square, take the square root.

pick.q: Make r the subject of A = πr².
e: Only r is squared: divide by π, then take the square root.
Take the square root of the whole of A ÷ π.
To undo a square, take the square root, do not square.
pick.y: Divide by π, then take the square root.

pick.q: Make v the subject of E = ½mv².
e: Only v is squared: undo it with a square root at the end.
Multiply by 2 to undo ½, do not divide.
To undo a square, take the square root.
pick.y: Multiply by 2, divide by m, then take the square root.

pick.q: Make x the subject of y = x² − k.
e: Add k first, then take the square root of the whole of y + k.
To undo a square, take the square root.
k is subtracted: add it to both sides.
pick.y: Add k to both sides, then take the square root.

cards.idea: After rearranging, substitute the values to find the new subject.

pick.q: Make t the subject of v = u + at.
e: a multiplies t: divide by a, do not subtract it.
u is added on the right: subtract it, do not add.
Subtract u first (it is added last), then divide by a.
pick.y: Subtract u from both sides, then divide by a.

pick.q: Make w the subject of P = 2l + 2w.
e: 2 multiplies w: divide by 2, do not subtract it.
2l is added: subtract it from both sides.
Divide the whole of P − 2l by 2.

pick.q: Make x the subject of y = mx + c.
e: m multiplies x: divide by m.
c is added: subtract it.
Subtract c first, then divide the whole of y − c by m.
pick.y: Subtract c, then divide by m.

pick.q: Make b the subject of A = ½(a + b)h.
e: Multiply by 2 to undo ½: 2A, then divide by h.
h multiplies the bracket: divide by h, do not subtract.
Divide by h, do not multiply.
pick.y: Multiply by 2, divide by h, then subtract a.

questions.prompt: v = u + at. Find t when v = {u + a * t}, u = {u} and a = {a}.

misconceptions.explain: That is v − u = at. Divide by a = {a} to find t.
Subtract u, do not add it.

pick.q: Make r the subject of A = πr².
e: Only r is squared: divide by π, then take the square root.
Take the square root of the whole of A ÷ π.
To undo a square, take the square root, do not square.
pick.y: Divide by π, then take the square root.

pick.q: Make v the subject of E = ½mv².
e: Only v is squared: undo it with a square root at the end.
Multiply by 2 to undo ½, do not divide.
To undo a square, take the square root.
pick.y: Multiply by 2, divide by m, then take the square root.

pick.q: Make x the subject of y = x² − k.
e: Add k first, then take the square root of the whole of y + k.
To undo a square, take the square root.
k is subtracted: add it to both sides.
pick.y: Add k to both sides, then take the square root.

questions.prompt: F = {9} ÷ {5} × C + {32}. Make C the subject and find C when F = {9 * n + 32}.

misconceptions.explain: Subtract {32} first, then multiply by {5} ÷ {9}: undo in reverse order.

pick.q: Make x the subject of ax + b = cx + d.
e: Move cx by subtracting it and b by subtracting it: signs change.
Factorise x(a − c), then divide by the whole bracket.
x is multiplied by (a − c): divide, do not subtract.
pick.y: Collect x terms: ax − cx = d − b, factorise x(a − c) = d − b, then divide.

pick.q: Make x the subject of y = (x + 1) ÷ (x − 1).
e: Check with y = 3: x = 2 gives (2 + 1) ÷ (2 − 1) = 3, so x = (y + 1) ÷ (y − 1).
x is a factor: factorise x(y − 1), then divide.
From xy − x = y + 1, x(y − 1) = y + 1: the signs are as in the answer.
pick.y: Multiply by (x − 1): xy − y = x + 1. Collect: xy − x = y + 1, so x(y − 1) = y + 1.

pick.q: Make a the subject of p = (a + b) ÷ a.
e: Divide b by the whole of (p − 1).
From pa = a + b: pa − a = b, so a(p − 1) = b.
Moving a to the left subtracts it: p − 1, not p + 1.
pick.y: Multiply by a: pa = a + b. Collect: pa − a = b, a(p − 1) = b.
